text: {"score":3,"justification":"Core numbers match the card (20.4% vs 2.7%, z 2.80, risk-adjusted 19.78, 45% low-complexity, ~423 excess, 30 documented claims, 4 documented 99215s, 6 of 22). The headline and the two cited claims are accurate, and the next steps are concrete. But the narrative is internally inconsistent and misleading in places, and the one unmatched number (8%) cannot be verified. The leaning of 'inconclusive' and 'random charts support the billed levels' sits uneasily with 'strongest signal' and 'top candidate for targeted review'. The 'blocked follow-up' claim has no evidence in the card. The next steps do not target the low-complexity 99215s that the rationale itself calls the top candidate, and the cited examples are only two low-complexity claims, with no documentation request for those visits.","problems":["The '8% for comparison providers' figure does not appear on the card; the card's all-provider rate for 99215 is 0.111 (11.1%), so the figure appears misread or unsupported.","The headline claims 'random charts support the billed levels', which overstates 4 documented 99215s; the records are not demonstrably random, and the rationale itself says the sample is thin.","The claim that a targeted follow-up 'was blocked because a request was already open' has no support in the evidence packet.","The next steps ask for a larger sample of 99214/99215 claims, not the low-complexity 99215s identified as the top candidate; this contradicts the rationale.","The rationale repeats the 6 of 22 finding twice and mixes the contradictory framings 'inconclusive', 'strongest signal' and 'top candidate'.","The claim that 'some notes may be written up to match the bill' is speculative; 'no lab on claim' does not show that data was not reviewed.","Only 2 example claims are cited out of 25 low-complexity 99215s, and none show the high-level contrast; the 0-condition examples are only partly informative (Z09 for a 99215)."]}
